Funding detail: Stipend covers standard UK salary and all university/institutional fees, with a budget for travel, conferences and equipment.

PhD Fellowship Overview

This 4-year PhD fellowship is part of the Novo Nordisk Foundation-funded project 'Deep Learning-Accelerated Crystallography Pipeline', a collaboration between Durham University, the University of Copenhagen, and the MAX IV synchrotron. The project aims to transform small-molecule structure determination by developing mathematical methods and integrating machine learning into crystallographic workflows.

Benefits & Coverage

  • Stipend covering standard UK salary
  • Full university/institutional fees
  • Budget for travel, conferences, and equipment
  • Four-year fixed-term position
  • Start date: 1 January 2027 or as soon as possible thereafter

Eligibility Criteria

  • Master's degree (or equivalent) in Chemistry, Mathematics, or Computer Science by the start of the PhD
  • Strong background in quantum crystallography and its underlying mathematical aspects
  • Adequate programming skills and willingness to apply machine learning
  • Open to UK and International students
  • English language proficiency (IELTS/TOEFL) required

Application Process

Submit a single PDF containing:

  1. CV (max. 2 pages)
  2. Cover letter (max. 1 page) describing motivation
  3. Certified copy of Master's diploma and transcript (with authorised English translation if required)
  4. Names and contact details of up to two referees
  5. Optional: link to repository with open-source scientific software contributions

Send applications to: norbert.peyerimhoff@durham.ac.uk and paul.n.ruth@durham.ac.uk

Deadline: 7 October 2026, 23:59 BST

Supervisors

  • Principal Supervisor: Professor Norbert Peyerimhoff, Department of Mathematical Sciences, Durham
  • Co-Supervisor: Dr Niklas Ruth, Advanced Research Computing (ARC), Durham

Key Tasks

  • Carry out independent research project under supervision
  • Complete PhD courses or equivalent training
  • Participate in research seminars
  • Disseminate results through visits, workshops, and conferences
  • Write a PhD thesis

Research Environment

Based in the Department of Mathematical Sciences at Durham University. Close collaboration with Professor Anders Østergaard Madsen at the University of Copenhagen and Dr Lennard Krause at MAX IV in Lund. Opportunities to interact with OlexSys.
